decision.question: children setter: route a config children: list through declare() without double-running it
options: call declare() eagerly from the children setter (runs during assign(), before naming() sets this.url, so children never get moved to the right url)
stage the raw list in this._raw_children from the setter; declare() (called once, by Page's constructor, after naming()) reads from that staged field
decision.chose: stage in _raw_children, declare() reads from there
decision.why: preserves the exact original ordering (naming() must run before children are added so they get the right url); a setter that calls declare() immediately would run before url exists and children would never move

decision.question: how a content LiveList and Sortable (ext/Draggable, out of fence) interoperate, since Sortable.release() hardcodes where.list.item.items.move(...)
options: modify Sortable.js to accept a configurable list-property name

give the content-list container's own Sortable wrapper item an .items alias pointing at the real content list, and give each row's Sortable the real content Item directly (so this.item.parent?.items safely resolves undefined on a Page, which makes LiveList.move() default source=this -- a correct same-list reorder)
decision.chose: alias on the container wrapper only, real Item on each row, no Sortable.js edit
decision.why: ext/Draggable/Sortable.js is not in this task's fence (not named in the brief's fence list) and is shared by Panel/editor; the alias confines the .items naming seam to Page.render_content_list() alone

log.msg: Grepped for page.listeners readers before deleting PageLog's own on/emit: only Log.js itself ever read it (Socket.js and ux/Dictate/floor.js have unrelated .listeners of their own). Safe to delete; on/off/emit now come from Item's Events mixin.

PageLog.Reader extends Item.Store, keeping open/close/parse/read/attach/changed/reset by name per the brief. attach() still holds-until-line-1 (slices off the first entry, already consumed by Page.jsonl() to build the page) before replaying the rest through Store.read(). Page.jsonl() now gets its reader via this.Reader.for(url+"page.jsonl") instead of `new this.Reader(...)`, so page.store (set by Store.attach) is the one shared instance per url.

Three real regressions found and fixed during the proof pass, none caught by node --check or the unit tests (all required a running browser + real app boot to surface): (1) naming() never actually set this.id despite its own comment claiming it did -- every add()-ed child was permanently unfindable by children.get()/.has(), reproduced via core/Page/generator/'s 'vtabs' child 404ing. (2) Page.jsonl()'s Store.for() caching (deliverable 4, as instructed) raced with load_all_children()'s own eager crawl of the same parent -- two concurrent calls for one url corrupted a shared reader's entries, 404ing a real page.jsonl page (core/Page/jsonl/) consistently. Fixed with an in-flight-promise guard. (3) the children setter only staged a config array/string for declare() and silently ignored a live `this.children = new Map()` reset (core/Page/generator/page.js's own grow(), which throws its whole tree away before rebuilding) -- old children never actually cleared. All three fixed, each re-verified, all 13 smoke pages re-run clean afterward.
